validation_method: Every lot car with a rule WMI, a 17-character VIN and a valid check digit is classified. The model year comes from VIN character 10 (the listing year only picks the 30-year cycle and must be within 2 years). A rule fires only when the VIN matches its WMI, years and fixed characters and its decision character is in its table for that year; other codes get no claim. Ground truth = scraper/manual_detect/ground_truth.jsonl; uniformCell lines are unlabelled, speeds-only lines are excluded, the rest are checkable: agree means (truth is manual) == (rule says manual). This family's VIN ground truth is almost all vPIC decodes of MY2017+ cars and AMC-era Jeeps (vPIC gives no Chrysler-format transmission before then) plus VIN-less listing lines, so only the AMC rules and the Renegade rule have checkable cars, and those are vPIC-derived (partly circular). Independent checks: (1) epa_rows, the EPA rows for the rule's exact model/engine (row ids; all must be the claimed class and every rule year must have a row); (2) a per-car EPA union check (year, the rule's make, feed/vPIC model names, vPIC displacement). Status: candidate (not counted) when flagged (transmission evidence contradicted, or the code's meaning comes only from vPIC) or when the EPA sole-offering check fails; drop when >= 20 checkable and agreement < 0.995; low_sample when < 20 checkable; keep otherwise. newly_confirmed_manual counts lot cars with no published transmission (vehicle_extras trans empty) that a keep or low_sample rule calls manual.

hub_findings.finding: vPIC returns the trim's standard transmission for FCA MY2018+ VINs, not the car's
hub_findings.evidence: 2018 Renegade Sport/Latitude with the 2.4L (engine B) decode as '6-spd Manual' although FCA Italy's MY2018 filing (ORG14586) makes B the 2.4L and EPA plus the Jeep press release make the 2.4L automatic-only; a 2021 Wrangler 2.0T decodes '6-spd Manual' although EPA lists only 'Automatic 8-spd' for the 2.0T (2019-2022). 2018 Compass Sport/Latitude 4x4, 2019 Challenger R/T and 2022 Gladiator Rubicon decode 'manual' where EPA lists both a manual and an automatic, so those labels are the standard transmission, not evidence about the car.
hub_findings.suggested_action: Hub decision (scraper change, not made here): drop the vPIC transmission for this family's MY2018+ decodes unless EPA lists only that transmission for the year/model/engine, and drop it where EPA contradicts it ('contradicted_by_epa'). The Renegade rule's automatic codes already contradict the 2.4L ones.

hub_findings.finding: The 1988 Wrangler 'uniform manual' cell is a VIN-encoded transmission, not a model default
hub_findings.evidence: AMC-era Jeep VINs carry the transmission in position 5 (Jeep Corporation filings 01-22-N11B-1748 and -1794). All six 1988 Wranglers on the lots have position 5 = V, which vPIC decodes as a 5-speed manual; V itself is not in any MID filing (the MY1988 base table is not in MID), so this worklist keeps V as a candidate and does not count it. Two of the six are 2.5L cars (2BCHV81S...), and EPA lists only a manual for the 1988 Wrangler 2.5L.
hub_findings.suggested_action: Keep the scraper's VPIC_TRANS_DEFAULT_CELLS entry for JEEP WRANGLER 1988 until a MY1987-1988 Jeep VIN table confirms V; the reason recorded there ('model-level default') should read 'VIN position 5 code not confirmed by a filing'.

hub_findings.finding: Chrysler encodes the transmission only on export VINs
hub_findings.evidence: Position 6 holds a transmission letter instead of the series digit on 'Europe Only' cars (MY1993 car table, 01-22-N11B-5018) and on BUX export vehicles with sales code ABB/YAB (MY2006 ORG467, MY2008 ORG6104, MY2009 ORG6105). Of the 22,946 lot VINs of this family for MY1993-2010, 7 have a letter in position 6; they look mistyped (WMIs such as '12D' and '204', a 1996 Ram 1500 'HFF13'), so none is read as an export transmission code and no rule uses this scheme.
